title: “Pipeline” by The Chantays
text: "Pipeline" is a surf rock instrumental by the Chantays, which was recorded in July 1962.

title: “Surf City” by Jan and Dean
text: "Surf City" is a 1963 song recorded by the American music duo Jan and Dean about a fictitious surf spot where there are "two girls for every boy". Written by Brian Wilson and Jan Berry, it was the first surf song to become a national number-one hit.

title: “It's My Party” by Lesley Gore
text: "It's My Party" is the debut song recorded by American singer Lesley Gore on her debut studio album I'll Cry If I Want To. It was released as her debut single on April 5, 1963, by Mercury Records.

title: “Blame It on the Bossa Nova” by Eydie Gormé
text: "Blame It on the Bossa Nova" is a song written by Cynthia Weil and Barry Mann that became a 1963 hit single for Eydie Gormé, reaching No. 7 on the Hot 100 in Billboard in March 1963.

title: “You Can't Sit Down” by The Dovells
text: "You Can't Sit Down" is a song originally recorded as an instrumental in 1959 as "Can't Sit Down" by the Bim Bam Boos, and popularized by the 1963 version by the Dovells, which included lyrics and vocals. The Dovells version of the song peaked at No.3 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and has been covered by many artists, including the Shangri-Las and Bruce Springsteen.

title: The Littlest Hobo
text: The Littlest Hobo is a Canadian television series based upon a 1958 American film of the same name directed by Charles R. Rondeau. The series first aired from 1963 to 1965 in syndication, and was revived for a popular second run on CTV, spanning six seasons, from October 11, 1979, to March 7, 1985.

title: The Forest Rangers
text: The Forest Rangers is a Canadian television series that ran from 1963 to 1965. It was a co-production between CBC Television and ITC Entertainment and was Canada's first television show produced in colour.

title: Elwood Glover's Luncheon Date
text: Elwood Glover's Luncheon Date is a Canadian talk show that aired on CBC Television from 1963 to 1975. Elwood Glover had hosted noon-time programming on CBC Radio since 1956.

title: Magistrate's Court
text: Magistrate's Court is a Canadian television series airing weekdays in syndication from 1963–1969 on the CBC. The show is a dramatization of the day-to-day life of a police magistrate, portrayed by Roy Jacques. The series was produced by Rai Purdy.
